clue.text: Poetry on loan includes one volume that's seditious

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece 'on' another sits after it, so the poetry follows the loan

parts.note: a sub is an advance or loan of money, as in 'sub me a tenner'

indicators.note: includes means the poetry word holds the next pieces within it

parts.note: verse is poetry
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dissident book of poems, lent out, carries a seditious message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts the one and the volume inside the poetry; 'on' in an across clue means that piece comes after the loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that aims to undermine established authority, a straight synonym.

clue.text: All there ignore nasty sandwiches served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the held letters are read upwards, backwards
the phrase ignore nasty sandwiches, or holds between its ends, a run of letters

explanation.surface: Someone of sound mind refuses unpleasant sandwiches offered to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' shows ENAS held across 'ignorE NASty'; 'served up' turns it into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: 'All there' is an idiom for mentally sound, rational and in possession of one's faculties.

clue.text: In Times, one cracking report

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the pieces before it go inside the report word

parts.note: a bang is a loud report, like a gunshot
T is the abbreviation for time, so times plural is TT
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A newspaper story in The Times breaks a report.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side that is 'in' is the one with the bat; the capital on 'In' hides that sense. 'cracking' puts both times and one inside the report.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a team or player that is in is currently at the crease, taking their innings.

clue.text: Buggy program not starting — see screen regularly displaying this?

definitions.text: Buggy program not starting — see screen regularly displaying this?

indicators.note: buggy software is faulty, so these letters are in a faulty, jumbled order
not starting means the first letter of program is dropped
regularly means every other letter of screen is taken, here the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A faulty program that won't start shows a warning on the monitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' leaves ROGRAM; 'regularly' takes SRE from 'screen'; with SEE, 'Buggy' rearranges the twelve letters. The whole clue also describes what such a program shows.
explanation.definitionFit: When buggy software fails to start, the screen typically shows a warning notice explaining the fault.

clue.text: Case for pedal stops considered for organ

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the pedal letters are lodged inside the next word

parts.note: seen as in 'seen as', regarded or considered

indicators.note: the case for a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A church organist pulls stops thought suitable for the pedal board.
explanation.walkthrough: The organ is a body part, not the instrument the stops and pedal suggest; 'stops' means plugs, lodging the case of pedal inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The spleen is an organ of the body, near the stomach, that filters blood.

clue.text: Title is the best part of thick books!

indicators.note: the best part of means most of, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: viscous means thick and sticky, like treacle
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A boast that the best part of something is its thick books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the best part of' means most of: the synonym for thick loses its last letter before the books are added.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a rank of the British peerage, so the word is itself a title of nobility.

clue.text: Back with little daughter's potty

parts.note: D is the short form of daughter
aft is the back part of a ship

explanation.surface: A toddler's potty is back, along with the little girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Potty is British slang for crazy or silly, a synonym of foolish.

clue.text: Criminal, one inside swallowed poison

indicators.note: inside means the criminal and one go within the next word

parts.note: ate means swallowed food
a con is a convict, a criminal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A criminal, inside prison, took poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal, one inside' looks like a convict in jail, but 'inside' is the insertion sign, putting the criminal and one within the word for swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, or monkshood, is a plant whose roots yield a deadly toxin.

clue.text: Vicar of Bray perhaps in issue over divorce? About right

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the issue word is read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to issue or send out

indicators.note: about means going round, so divorce surrounds right

parts.note: to sever is to divorce or separate

explanation.surface: A clergyman at the centre of a dispute about divorce asks whether he's right.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray, in an English folk song, kept his parish by switching faith with each monarch. 'over' turns the issue word round; 'About' wraps divorce round right.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shifts loyalties to suit those in power is an opportunist, and the song's vicar is the classic example.

clue.text: One barely seen around Australia, having left Darwin?

indicators.note: around means the nudist goes round the next letters

parts.note: a naturist is a nudist, someone seen bare

explanation.surface: A nudist wanders around Australia before leaving the city of Darwin.
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin looks like the Australian city, which fits the surface; it is Charles Darwin. 'around' puts A and L inside NATURIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin studied plants and animals, an example of a student of the natural world.

clue.text: Create possibilities for sex?

definitions.meaning: on an official document, sex is marked female or male, the letters ..., a playful reading of the word

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what makes the creation of new possibilities in sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The box on a document asking your sex offers two letters with 'or' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To form something is to make, shape or bring it into being, a synonym of produce.

clue.text: Opera buff supporting first of ideas to cut price, say? Not quite

indicators.note: to cut means to break into, so the idea letter and the buff go inside the other pieces

parts.note: cost is price

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the buff comes after
first of means only the opening letter of ideas is used

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a fan

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter of the joined words is dropped

parts.note: to utter is to say

explanation.surface: An opera enthusiast backs an idea to cut ticket prices, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims COSTUTTER to COSTUTTE; 'to cut' places IFAN inside it after COS. Così fan tutte is Mozart's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Così fan tutte is a comic opera by Mozart, so the title names an example of the form.

clue.text: Study of domestic finances or cosmic income shifts

indicators.note: shifts means the letters of the preceding words move into a new order

explanation.surface: Household finances are studied, or perhaps the shifts of a cosmic income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' rearranges all fourteen letters of 'or cosmic income'.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of economics studies individual households and firms rather than whole national economies.

clue.text: I'll break arm getting lid off? That's an original thought

indicators.note: break means the I bursts into the arm word

parts.note: a branch is an arm, as of a tree or organisation
I'll is I will: the I is what breaks in, the 'll saying it will

indicators.note: off means the letters of lid are put out of order

explanation.surface: A boast about smashing an arm while trying to remove a lid, hailed as a bright idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Arm here is a branch, not a limb; only the I of I'll breaks in, and 'off' scrambles lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's own invention or idea is called their creation, the child of their mind.

clue.text: Wearing a hairpiece? That's rough

definitions.meaning: a rug is slang for a toupee, so someone in one is playfully described this way
craggy and uneven, as a coastline or a face

explanation.surface: A remark that a man in a toupee looks rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough and craggy terrain or features are described this way, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Mastermind born in turbulent reign

indicators.note: in means the born word goes inside the rearranged letters
turbulent means stormy and disordered, so the letters of reign are jumbled

parts.note: née, born, introduces a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A criminal mastermind is born into a turbulent reign.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind looks like a noun but is a verb here; 'turbulent' jumbles reign, and 'in' puts born inside those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer a plan is to contrive and organise it, as a mastermind does.

clue.text: Refined young society woman broadcasting

parts.note: a deb, debutante, is a young woman making her debut in high society
a show being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A refined debutante who presents on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave, polished and elegant, close in sense to sophisticated.

clue.text: Fake claim by online commenter?

indicators.note: by means beside, so the claim sits next to the commenter

parts.note: the claim is 'I'm', what someone says when asserting who they are
a poster is someone who posts comments on an online forum

explanation.surface: A fake claim made by someone commenting on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: The commenter's claim reads 'I'm poster'. The ending -er is a recognised variant of -or for this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud pretending to be someone else is a fake, a synonym of charlatan.

clue.text: Gas is primarily poor conductor

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of poor is used

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British orchestral conductor

explanation.surface: A science-sounding claim that gas is a poor conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: Gas looks like a noun of physics; here it is a verb meaning chatter. Simon Rattle led the Berlin Philharmonic and London Symphony orchestras.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas, in informal use, is to chatter idly at length, a synonym of babble.

clue.text: Bog area oddly contains river grubs

indicators.note: contains means the bog and area letters hold the river within them

parts.note: bog and lav are both British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of area, the first and third

explanation.surface: A marshy area holds a river teeming with grubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog suggests marshland, but it is the slang for a lavatory. 'oddly' takes AE from 'area'; 'contains' puts R inside LAVAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubs are insect young in their worm-like stage, an example of the immature forms.

clue.text: Wagon with difficulty goes over a plain

indicators.note: in a down clue the wagon pieces go over, above, the letter A

parts.note: a van is a wagon, as a railway goods wagon
ill means with difficulty, as in 'can ill afford'

explanation.surface: A wagon struggles across a plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain looks like a flat landscape, but it is an adjective meaning ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is informal for ordinary or basic, with no extras, like the plain ice-cream flavour.

clue.text: Fed up with one blemish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word fed is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: Someone sick of having just one blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: Fed up looks like an idiom for sick of, but 'up' reverses fed in this down clue; blemish is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To blemish something is to spoil its surface or appearance, a verb sense close to disfigure.

clue.text: How to get nun to see and adopt a different opinion?

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says rearrange the letters of 'ones tune', which gives the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A question on how to get a nun to see things another way.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, would shuffle ONES TUNE into the letters of NUN TO SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to alter one's view or attitude, usually suddenly and conveniently.

clue.text: The speaker's filled a convention

indicators.note: the speaker's means as the speaker says it, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: packed means filled, as a full suitcase or hall

explanation.surface: The speaker has filled a convention hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Convention suggests a conference, but it is an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A convention, in the diplomatic sense, is a formal agreement between states, a synonym of treaty.

clue.text: Return nine letters — one from Thessaly

indicators.note: return means the run of letters is turned back to front

parts.note: the letters A to I make nine letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An instruction to send back nine letters, one of them from Thessaly in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The span A to I covers nine letters; 'Return' reverses A TO I. Fittingly, the answer is the ninth Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thessaly is a region of Greece, so one of its letters is a character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Steps aren't at all rickety

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and unsteady, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A reassurance that a flight of stairs is not at all wobbly.
explanation.walkthrough: Steps suggests a staircase, but it means a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a lively Italian folk dance, and steps can mean a dance.

clue.text: Extending far underground, weed comes back

indicators.note: comes back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: wee is slang for urinate, so weed means peed

explanation.surface: A garden weed with roots reaching far underground keeps returning.
explanation.walkthrough: Weed looks like a garden plant but is the past tense of wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reaching a long way down below the surface is profound, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Not apt to decamp, putting Irish corps first

indicators.note: first means the Irish corps are placed ahead of the decamp word

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army
to levant is a British slang word for running off without paying debts

explanation.surface: Irish soldiers who are not inclined to desert are sent in first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apt to decamp' reads as a tendency, but 'Not apt' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beside the point or unrelated is not pertinent, a synonym of immaterial.
